title: Minimum Operations to Make Columns Strictly Increasing
summary: Given a m x n matrix grid consisting of non-negative integers, determine the minimum number of operations required to make each column strictly increasing.
statement: Given a m x n matrix grid consisting of non-negative integers, determine the minimum number of operations required to make each column strictly increasing. In one operation, you can increment the value of any grid[i][j] by 1.
constraints: You may increment any grid cell by one per operation.
Make every column strictly increasing from top to bottom.
Return the minimum total number of increments.
hints: Scan downward while tracking the already adjusted previous value.
Raise the current cell only to max(original, previous+1).
Any smaller value violates strict increase and any larger value wastes operations, proving the greedy choice optimal.
editorial: Any smaller value violates strict increase and any larger value wastes operations, proving the greedy choice optimal.

tests.explanation: Raising each cell only to one above its adjusted predecessor requires fifteen increments total.
Both columns are already strictly increasing, so zero operations are needed.
